title: Four jobs, four tools
scenario:
You are the designer on a launch for a new oat-milk brand. The brief has four jobs:

1. A hero image of the carton on a kitchen table.
2. An 8-second vertical teaser with sound.
3. A voice-over script read in English and Spanish.
4. A check of 40 photos from shops: is the carton's logo facing the front?

Your studio has four AI tools. The exhibit lists what each one reads and makes, copied from the vendors' docs.
exhibit:
Studio tool list (input -> output, from each vendor's docs)

Tool A  text + image          -> text
Tool B  text + images (refs)  -> image  (generate and edit)
Tool C  text or images        -> 8-second video with audio
Tool D  text only             -> audio (speech, up to 2 speakers)

questions.prompt: Which tool should do job 4, the logo check on 40 shop photos?

options.text: Tool A, because it reads images and writes text, and the result you need is a written report.
options.explanation: Right. Job 4 needs a model that looks at photos and reports. That is image in, text out, like Claude's vision.

options.text: Tool B in edit mode, so it can circle the logo on each photo.
options.explanation: Edit mode still outputs an image. Job 4 needs a written report you can count, which is image in, text out.

options.text: Tool C, because 40 photos are like the frames of a video.
options.explanation: Tool C makes video. It does not write a report on photos you give it.

options.text: None of them. Only a person can look at photos.
options.explanation: Vision models read images and answer in text. A person should still spot-check, but Tool A fits the job.

questions.prompt: A teammate asks Tool A to "make the hero image" and gets no image. What is the reason?

options.explanation: A longer prompt does not change what a model can output. Tool A outputs text only.

options.text: Tool A's output is text. A model that reads images does not always make them.
options.explanation: Right. The Claude vision docs say Claude is an image understanding model only and cannot generate images. Read the output side of a tool first.

options.text: Tool A is broken and needs a restart.
options.explanation: Nothing is broken. Tool A is working as documented: image and text in, text out.

options.text: The teammate needs to upload a reference photo first.
options.explanation: A reference image is still input. Tool A's output stays text, whatever you give it.

questions.prompt: For job 3, what do you give Tool D?

options.text: The finished teaser video, so it can match the voice to the picture.
options.explanation: The exhibit says Tool D reads text only. Google's speech docs say these models take text-only input.

options.text: A mood board image, so it picks the right tone.
options.explanation: Tool D can't read images. Describe the tone in words instead.

options.text: Nothing. It writes the script and the voice on its own.
options.explanation: Tool D turns your text into speech. You still bring the script.

options.text: The written script, in English and in Spanish.
options.explanation: Right. A speech model takes text and makes audio. The script is your input.
